extracted.intended_audience: general readers, Texas residents, donors, partner newsrooms, prospective journalists and staff
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational editorial standards and operational policies for a nonprofit, digital-first newsroom (The Texas Tribune), covering accuracy, sourcing, conflicts of interest, sponsorships, data practices, corrections, and public engagement. Intended to guide journalists, partners, donors and readers on how the organization produces and governs its journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission / Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: We pursue the truth so Texans can shape our future. The Tribune is a nonpartisan, nonprofit digital-first media organization covering Texas politics, government and public policy to increase civic engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vision: enable self-government through accurate information so Texans can ask questions, hold leaders accountable and participate in shaping policy agendas across political/geographic divides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and Attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Our reporting on all platforms will be truthful, transparent and respectful; our facts will be accurate, complete and fairly presented. Our analysis will represent our best independent judgment, not our preferences or those of our sources. There will be no hidden agendas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tribune journalists will not republish stories, images or other content from outside sources without permission and credit. Plagiarism, fabrication and misappropriation of intellectual property are all grounds for immediate termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections policy
rubrics_metrics.description: When we make a mistake we will work quickly to fully address the error, correcting it within the story, detailing the error on the story page and adding it to a running list of Tribune corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you find an error, email corrections@texastribune.org. The organization will be transparent about the magnitude of errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: We investigate claims with skepticism; challenge conventional wisdom; consult data to verify claims by public officials; and confirm information with experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff constantly assess whether information is verified and trustworthy, may share relevant components of a story with a primary source or an outside expert to verify them, and are expected to verify and double-check information through interviews, research, data collection and data analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing and anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune will try to identify all sources, granting anonymity only when the information is critical to the story, the source is reliable and there is no other way to obtain the information. Senior editorial leaders must approve anonymous sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not say a person declined comment if they are already quoted anonymously. Identify in reporting any bias we know our sources have. Anonymous sources should know the reporter will share their identity with a senior editor, who will keep it confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: No deceptive newsgathering / source misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Our journalists will never misrepresent themselves or mislead a source to get an interview or a story, and they will always identify themselves as journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters do not use hidden cameras or microphones, go undercover or pay for interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decisions are made by journalists alone. Funders and donors do not entitle them to preferential treatment or relationships with newsroom staff and do not protect them from investigation or scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions are published by year and amount. Journalists should avoid investments or work on stories in which they have a vested financial or personal interest. Secondary employment or freelance work must be cleared by an editor. Employees, contractors and interns will refrain from partisan political activity, including political contributions or displaying partisan signage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of donor/sponsor relationships in coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that reference or quote a Tribune donor or corporate sponsor who has contributed $1,000 or more will include a written disclosure when those stories are picked up by other news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundraisers must inform potential donors that contributions do not entitle them to editorial influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts, honoraria and outside payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees, contractors and interns will not accept any gift with more than a nominal value from any company, individual or institution that could have an interest in the Tribune’s reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial employees may speak at events or moderate panels so long as the role is purely journalistic; any honoraria must be paid to the Tribune — not to the journalist — as a tax-deductible donation. Staff always pay their own way when traveling for editorial or business purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorships, advertising and paid content separation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune accepts corporate sponsorships, underwriting and advertising that do not compromise editorial integrity. All paid content must be clearly and obviously distinguished from editorial content and visually differentiated; sponsors play no role in editorial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor or advertiser messages that contain false or unlawful content or that undermine the Tribune's integrity may be removed. All corporate support will be solicited by business staff and no sponsored content will be produced by Texas Tribune employees. Present and past sponsors are listed by amount and year. Paid content is labeled 'paid content.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Externally funded but editorially independent content
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes the Tribune seeks out content supported by funding from an entity; this content is independently produced by our journalists and not approved or reviewed by the funding entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such content will include a note that it was supported by another organization to make the funding relationship transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo, video and audio integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Photo editors and video producers may improve the technical quality of photos and video or audio recordings, but may not alter the substance of that media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All photo illustrations, graphics or animations will be clearly labeled as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Republishing and partnerships policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune provides all of its news and information to Texas newspapers, news sites, radio and television stations to republish for free, with a few ground rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization frequently collaborates with other nonprofit newsrooms and encourages partnerships that make sense — e.g., combining subject mastery and the Tribune's sourcing/context. The Tribune is a member of the Institute for Nonprofit News and lists significant editorial partnerships (e.g., ProPublica-Texas Tribune investigative unit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data publishing and public databases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune is an authoritative source of user-friendly databases of public information and collaborates between journalists and software engineers to present a full picture for readers using data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include government salaries database, tool for finding political districts, and elected officials directory; data is presented to help readers be more thoughtful, productive and engaged residents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Events openness and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Events are on-the-record, open-to-the-public and often available via livestream with archived videos posted online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Tribune hosts dozens of events annually in many venues and publishes/archives event videos; signature event is The Texas Tribune Festival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to inclusion and representative coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune seeks to ensure its newsroom and news coverage reflects Texas by including a wide range of perspectives from people of different backgrounds, ideologies and experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion is presented as integral to serving Texans and building trust across communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to external journalistic codes and evolving policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune borrows generously from policies of other nonprofit news organizations and adheres to the Code of Ethics of the Society of Professional Journalists (seek truth, minimize harm, act independently, be accountable and transparent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies will be revised as the industry and technology evolve. Exceptional circumstances may require exceptions to rules and require editorial leadership recalibration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial transparency and public reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune is supported by a diversified business model (membership, major donations, corporate sponsorships, events, paid newsletter and other revenue) and is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization. Editorial decisions are made by journalists alone and are not influenced by donors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Tribune provides financial statements and annual reports to the public (e.g., Organizational Overview, Audit Report) and posts a full list of financial documents and contributions by year and amount.
